featureHighlights.label: Moisture lands where you're brushing
featureHighlights.body: The spray outlet sits in the brush head, so mist reaches the strands you're working on — not the mirror. Dry lengths get hydration exactly as you detangle them, which helps calm frizz and static.

image.altText: Close-up of fine mist spraying from the brush head onto hair

featureHighlights.label: Use the leave-in you already love
featureHighlights.body: The refillable top-fill tank takes plain water or a light hair serum and releases it as an even mist rather than drips — so a little product goes further and doesn't sit heavy on your roots.

image.altText: Pouring hair serum into the brush's top-fill mist tank

featureHighlights.label: A scalp massage with every pass
featureHighlights.body: Rounded, flexible bristle tips on an air cushion press gently against the scalp. Relaxing at the end of a long day, and gentle enough for everyday brushing.

image.altText: Woman brushing near her scalp with the beige Elecspray brush

featureHighlights.label: Clean bristles in one press
featureHighlights.body: Every brush collects hair. Press the release button and the bristle plate pushes it up and out, ready to wipe away — no picking strands out with your fingers.

image.altText: Self-cleaning in one press: collected hair is pushed off the bristles

benefits.label: Mist as you brush
benefits.body: A fine spray hydrates strands while the bristles move through them.

benefits.label: Less pulling
benefits.body: Cushioned, flexible bristles give at knots instead of tearing through.

benefits.label: Self-cleaning
benefits.body: One press pushes trapped hair off the bristles.

story.label: Still fighting frizz and knots every morning?
story.body: A dry brush drags through tangles, builds static and leaves flyaways standing up. Adding a spray bottle means juggling two things at once — and the brush still ends up clogged with hair.

story.label: Meet the Elecspray Hair Brush.
story.body: It puts the mist inside the brush. Fill the tank with water or your favourite light leave-in, press once, and a fine spray reaches your hair as the cushioned bristles glide through — hydrated and detangled in the same stroke. When you're done, one press clears the bristles.

image.altText: Woman brushing long, smooth hair as the brush releases a fine mist

howItWorks.body: Open the port on top and add water or a light, water-thin leave-in.

howItWorks.label: Mist & brush
howItWorks.body: Switch it on and brush from the ends up to the roots as the fine mist releases.

howItWorks.label: Clean
howItWorks.body: Press the release button to push collected hair off the bristles, then wipe away.

useCases.body: Revive bed-head and smooth flyaways in a couple of minutes before you head out.

useCases.label: Evening wind-down

whatsIncluded.label: 1 × Elecspray Hair Brush
whatsIncluded.body: In your chosen colour, with built-in rechargeable battery and refillable mist tank.

faq.question: What can I put in the tank?
faq.answer: Plain water works for everyday frizz and static. You can also use a light, water-thin leave-in serum or essence. Avoid thick creams and heavy oils — if a product won't mist from an ordinary spray bottle, it won't mist from the brush either.

faq.question: Does it need batteries?
faq.answer: No. It runs on a built-in 300 mAh rechargeable battery, so there's nothing to replace — just recharge it when it runs low.

faq.question: Will it work on my hair type?
faq.answer: The flexible cushioned bristles are made to glide through straight, wavy, curly and thick hair. For very tight curls or heavy knots, work in small sections and start from the ends.

faq.question: How do I clean it?
faq.answer: Press the release button to push collected hair off the bristles and wipe it away. If you won't use it for a few days, empty the tank, and keep the charging port dry.

faq.question: Which colour should I choose?
faq.answer: Beige, pink and purple are the same brush with identical features — it's purely your preference. Selecting a colour switches the main photo so you can see it.

faq.question: How long does shipping take, and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Delivery options and the exact cost for your address are shown at checkout before you pay. Every order gets a tracking link once the carrier scans it.

faq.question: Can I return it?
faq.answer: Yes — within 30 days of receiving it. Because it's a personal-care item, it needs to be unused and in its original packaging. Email support@shoptrackify.com to start a return and we'll send you a return label.

products.description: An acupressure pen you can actually check the specs on. Most listings in this category tell you what the device will do for your body. This one tells you what it is: a 158 g pen in an ABS and aluminium-alloy body, nine intensity levels on a lit display, five screw-on heads, and a single AA cell. Press the tip to a point, pick a level, and that is the whole machine.. What you actually get Five heads, oil-free — rounded ball, ridged, fine point and flat spoon, plus the fitted tip on the pen. Every head is in the box. None is held back as a paid extra. Nine levels, held on the display — the level you set stays on screen until you change it, so the setting that suited you yesterday is the one you return to, not a guess at the same number of button presses. Auto point-sensing tip — the tip responds as it passes over an active point, so you do not need a meridian chart memorised before you start. One AA cell — no charger, no cable, no charging cradle, and no battery that dies at three years old and takes the device with it. It travels in hand luggage without an argument. 170 mm, 158 g — long enough to reach between your own shoulder blades one-handed, light enough to hold there. Honest specifications Body: ABS and aluminium alloy Weight: 158 g, oil-free build, without packaging Heads: five, interchangeable, threaded (not friction-fit) Intensity: nine selectable levels Power: one AA cell, not included What it is, and what it is not This is a consumer wellness and massage tool that applies pressure through a metal tip along with a low-level electrical pulse, in the same broad family as the TENS units sold in any pharmacy. It is not a medical device. It is not cleared by the FDA or Health Canada, and nothing here is a health claim or a treatment for any condition. If a listing for one of these tells you it cures something, that is the moment to close the tab. Do not use it if you have a pacemaker or any implanted electronic device, or if you are pregnant. Avoid broken skin, the front and sides of the neck, and the area near the eyes. If you have a heart condition, epilepsy or reduced sensation, ask a doctor first. Common questions Do I need to know the pressure points first?No. The auto-sensing tip responds as it passes over an active point, which is what most people use to find where to work. How long should a session be?Five to fifteen minutes across a few points, once or twice a day. Longer is not better. If a spot goes numb, sore or red, stop and move on. What is the difference between the heads?The fine point concentrates on one spot, the ball and spoon spread the same pressure over a wider area, and the ridged head suits a broad muscle like a calf or a forearm. Is a battery included?No. It takes one standard AA cell, which keeps the pen cheap to run and legal to fly with.

  • One AA cell — no charger, no cable, no charging cradle, and no battery that dies at three years old and takes the device with it. It travels in hand luggage without an argument.
  • 170 mm, 158 g — long enough to reach between your own shoulder blades one-handed, light enough to hold there.

Honest specifications

  • Body: ABS and aluminium alloy
  • Weight: 158 g, oil-free build, without packaging
  • Heads: five, interchangeable, threaded (not friction-fit)
  • Intensity: nine selectable levels
  • Power: one AA cell, not included

What it is, and what it is not

This is a consumer wellness and massage tool that applies pressure through a metal tip along with a low-level electrical pulse, in the same broad family as the TENS units sold in any pharmacy. It is not a medical device. It is not cleared by the FDA or Health Canada, and nothing here is a health claim or a treatment for any condition. If a listing for one of these tells you it cures something, that is the moment to close the tab.

Do not use it if you have a pacemaker or any implanted electronic device, or if you are pregnant. Avoid broken skin, the front and sides of the neck, and the area near the eyes. If you have a heart condition, epilepsy or reduced sensation, ask a doctor first.

Common questions

Do I need to know the pressure points first?
No. The auto-sensing tip responds as it passes over an active point, which is what most people use to find where to work.

How long should a session be?
Five to fifteen minutes across a few points, once or twice a day. Longer is not better. If a spot goes numb, sore or red, stop and move on.

What is the difference between the heads?
The fine point concentrates on one spot, the ball and spoon spread the same pressure over a wider area, and the ridged head suits a broad muscle like a calf or a forearm.

Is a battery included?
No. It takes one standard AA cell, which keeps the pen cheap to run and legal to fly with.
